title: bf16/f16 MACC draft contract
boundary: Actual lower_bf16_matmul_f32acc input/output, including its optional lower_model entry invocation.
example:
+0-initialized half matrix product
→ extend operands to f32
→ accumulate in original order
→ truncate once to the original half format
claim: Complete equality to the source-derived draft reference and strict nonempty local-site qualification. Numerical approval remains abstracted; no original-source equivalence claim.
proof:
MerlinVerify.Check.Bf16F32AccBoundary.check_sound
Exact reference + strict sites + complete source denominator
limit: Explicit selection only; excluded from all. Matching bf16 or f16 formats, checked +0 initialization and maps. Mixed source formats and nonzero initialization refuse. title: Ordered unrolling

example:
Dynamic outer loop stays in place.
Its inner 5 iterations become 2 groups × 2 lanes + 1 tail.
Zero outer trips still execute no inner work.
claim: Equal returned values, modeled errors and terminal world, under the common scalar/SCF interpretation.
limit: Explicit one-based depth; static selected index64 controls, arbitrary supported dynamic ancestors and partial calls. Actual combined inner-depth qualification now preserves deeper dynamic bodies, with native checks, fresh replay and real Lean callee/stride refusals. Actual source strides remain known positive. Resource limits apply.

title: Ordered tiling
boundary: The actual source loop → ordered one-dimensional segments. Runs alone or after unrolling.
example:
7 groups
→ segments [3, 3, 1]
A short final segment retains the original order.
claim: Scalar route: equal returns, modeled errors and terminal world. Memory route: the whole storage chain's successful-observation relation.
limit: Depth is selected at the actual tiling stage after unrolling. Public inner TILE and combined UNROLL→TILE gates/native controls pass with exact intermediate/output custody. Retained deeper-body captures are qualified through the controlled auxiliary projection; actual source stride checks remain strict. Private-buffer tiles permit size2–65,536 under a finite resource policy; signed-index64 safety is checked separately.

title: Private buffer reuse
boundary: Original → shape-normalized → reused, with an optional fourth actual segmented output.
interface:
Options(buffer_allocator='total_private_unobservable')
--validate-passes buffer_reuse
# Optional tile_size=2 additionally selects initializer segmentation.
example:
Allocate A → initialize → use → free
Allocate B → initialize → use → free
→ reuse one private slot for both lifetimes
claim: Equal sets of possible successful public observations under the explicitly selected total, private, unobservable allocator model.
limit: Static rank-two i8/i16/i32/i64 rectangular initialization, sequential disjoint private lifetimes. Untiled and tiled actual outputs have proof routes. Explicit total/private/unobservable allocator; no finite-capacity, complete failure-state or native allocator proof. Additive rank-one uniform-seed bridges pass all 33 installed host/compiler/native/replay/mutation cases, including both public routes, fresh-process replay and classified target/component refusals. Default-all memory composition now passes actual untiled and tiled32-tail compiler gates, with a separate complete successful-return/world DCE proof and authentic unchanged CSE observation. Changed memory CSE still refuses. Computed prefixes and rank-three source bridges remain engineering.

title: Dead-code elimination
boundary: Exact IR immediately before and after the compiler's preprocessing pruning.
example:
%dead = tensor.empty()
%answer = arith.addi %a, %b
return %answer
→ erase %dead
Memory route: unused index literal + retained memref/SCF work
→ the same complete entry without that unused literal.
claim: Strict tensor-stage refinement on inputs of the declared types, with source support established. Original memory route: equality of complete successful returned-value/world relations for actual dead index-constant deletions.
limit: Only modeled effect-free tensor/scalar operations may be erased. Numerical preparation and native lowering are separate boundaries. The memory rule retains partial actions, casts, dimensions and regions; no categorized-error or divergence equivalence. Actual default-all untiled and tile32-tail routes pass.

title: Q/DQ proposed-model refinement

Q/DQ source operations
→ specified ordered scalar expansion

limit: Explicit-only proposed source model, outside all. Pinned producer/Torch native source capture has been qualified. Optional proved prefix composes captured IR through final output and reopens foreign sources after composition. Definedness, broader source formats and independent semantic approval remain open. Conditional quantizer definedness is proved under an explicit conversion condition; concrete PyTorch/IEEE fidelity remains open.

title: Common-subexpression elimination
boundary: The leading CSE in the build's actual runner, before tensor bufferization. Original memory route binds the actual upstream input, pipeline, runner and CSE pair.
claim: Strict tensor-stage refinement; operand aliases and captured region values are checked.
limit: The trailing CSE after lowering to LLVM dialect is not this gate. Unsupported SCF/memory inputs are not silently covered by the tensor checker. Authentic unchanged memory CSE submits zero jobs and receives zero proof credit; changed, missing and skip-only memory captures refuse. Canonicalization remains a separate boundary.
